title: Crestline retail integration - field digest
notes:
Meeting capture - quick field digest (working notes)

Date: 2025-11-03 11:00 PT (45m)
Participants: Crestline: Jamie Ortega (Head of Integrations), Ravi Patel (Platform eng), Lena Wu (Retail analytics) -- Redwood: Priya Kapoor (SE), Evan Liu (Infra), Marisol Vega (SRE advisor)

High-level goal
- Crestline wants a cashier-assist and returns triage assistant that uses store receipts + basic inventory context to: classify returns, suggest refund vs replace, and auto-fill claim forms. The main constraint is PCI/PII minimization + sub-200ms 90th pct latency for the inline cashier flow.

Business success metrics (customer-specified)
- Reduction in manual return triage time by 50% within 8 weeks of pilot
- False-action rate < 3% (i.e., suggested refunds that were wrong)
- Cost target: operating cost for inference not to exceed $0.0009 per inference on average (they gave a top-level cap).

Traffic profile + data shape
- 20 qps steady for pilot store set (50 stores), bursts up to 250 qps during promos.
- Typical payload: OCRed receipt text (~150-700 tokens after OCR cleanup), optional JSON inventory snippet (small).
- Upstream latency budget from their POS: 300ms end-to-end; Redwood portion target <=200ms 90p for inline API path.

Security / compliance notes
- Must ensure no raw card numbers stored or sent to hosted inference. They will mask PANs at OCR stage. Need SAML SSO for console access and RBAC for routes.
- Crestline requires KMS integration for encryption-at-rest of logs and a purge policy (30 days) for any PII-derived traces. They asked about HSM options for Private deployment.

Initial architecture preferences from customer
- Prefer Redwood Private (VPC) because they want privacy and to keep logs inside AWS account, but open to Redwood Dedicated if the Private timeline is too long.
- VPC peering + private link are acceptable. They want host-based egress controls to block external vector DB calls (they plan to use internal Chroma/Weaviate).

Technical gotchas called out during call (important)
1) OCR noise: receipt OCR often puts line breaks and odd tokens (item codes like "SKU#A-12/34"). Need prompt engineering + tokenization-aware preprocessing to avoid prompt explosions. Suggest a small pre-clean step in their POS edge before sending.
2) Multilingual receipts: ~12% spanish partial entries; model must handle mixed-lingual snippets. Recommend model that has robust multilingual support (avoid tiny english-only models).
3) Atomicity: cashier flow is synchronous; cannot block for long-running rerank/embedding ops. If they want logging + batch quality checks, we should offload to async workflows.
4) Embeddings usage: they want to surface historical receipt matches for fraud/returns. That means embeddings + vector DB; confirm firewall rules to allow calls from private subnets only.
5) Edge token limits: some receipts are long (e.g., long grocery orders) - define a hard truncate and a fallback summary policy.

Suggested Redwood config (quick sketch for PoC)
- Deployment: start PoC on Dedicated (reserved small pool) for fastest turnaround; plan parallel Private migration in sprint 3.
- Model: mid-sized open model with multilingual support; enable quantized variant for Dedicated to reduce cost.
- SLOs: configure 90th pct latency target 200ms, with a canary route that uses a slightly smaller model for spikes.
- Runtime features: enable prefix caching for repeated receipt templates; KV cache for chat-style follow-ups; 30ms batching window (aggressive) with max batch size 64 for high throughput paths.
- Observability: token-level cost + latency tracing on per-route dashboards. Materialize a per-store dashboard for top 10 error types.

PoC scope (MVP) - 6 weeks
1) Integration adapter in their staging to send OCR text + inventory snippet to Redwood hosted endpoint.
2) Baseline model evaluation: run 1k labeled receipts (Crestline to provide) against candidate models; measure accuracy and latency.
3) Real-time cashier API route + async logging pipeline to vector DB for historical matching.
4) Security review + KMS integration stub
5) Short eval harness (automated tests for 100 common return scenarios).

Open questions we promised to follow up on
- Can Crestline provide a sanitized sample dataset (500 receipts) by EOW 11/07? They said yes but need an NDA addendum for sample.
- Which vector DB vendor will they run in VPC? They mentioned Chroma but procurement might prefer Milvus. Need specifics for egress allowed IPs/ports.
- Exact SAML metadata for SSO (they will gather).
- Expected peak token size in worst-case receipts (they'll run a histogram and send numbers).
- Legal: do they want Redwood to store any log-derived labels? They prefer not to; will confirm.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Priya: create PoC plan + ticket in GitHub repo, include minimal prompt set and candidate model list (due 2025-11-07).
- Evan: draft Dedicated reservation sizing & cost estimate (two sizing points: steady 20 qps, burst 250 qps) (due 2025-11-10).
- Marisol: security checklist + KMS/HSM options memo; include Private migration checklist (due 2025-11-10).
- Jamie (Crestline): share sanitized sample set + confirm vector DB choice (target 2025-11-07).

Quick notes from the whiteboard (informal)
- If cost target is hard, explore a hybrid: small Dedicated pool for low-latency inline + fallback to a cheaper quantized model for high-volume background classification.
- Consider prompt templates that extract structured fields first (item list, totals, tax, return reason) then pass structured JSON to the decision model to reduce token count.
- Add a small RAG-free classifier that runs on embeddings of item lines for quick matching to historical fraud signatures (cheap, local).

Risks to monitor
- If OCR masking fails, PCI leakage risk; require strict validation and masked sampling in staging.
- Latency spikes from vector DB lookups if DB is misconfigured - ensure timeouts and circuit breaker on DB calls.
- Model regression on edge cases (coupons, split-tenders) - build a prompt/eval set with those cases.

Notes to self (things to remember in follow-ups)
- Use the existing Crestline slack thread for small questions (quickest path).
- Add a lightweight eval job in CI to compute false-action rate nightly (target <3%).
- Keep a short list of fallback prompts that are shorter and cheaper for high-volume windows.

End of digest - this is a working capture, will convert to a formal PoC brief once sample data and SSO/KMS details are in.

-- Priya
